summary: @cdnshell/loader ships an obfuscated fetch-and-eval loader plus a versioned iOS/macOS implant kit
details: The package presents itself as a static-asset distribution loader but its single JavaScript module `a12i5u6l.js` is a heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style rotated string array, `_0xXXXX` symbol renames, base64+URI-decoded string table) fetch-and-eval loader. On evaluation it installs itself on `globalThis` behind a `Symbol.for(...)` slot and runs a bootstrap that (a) `atob`-decodes two embedded ~10KB base64 blobs and executes them via `new Function(atob(...))()`, and (b) `fetch()`es further modules from a caller-supplied `base` URL and passes the response body to `new Function(text)()` — a direct remote-code-execution primitive. The tarball also ships an offensive-implant kit under `03_payloads/`: iOS-major-version-indexed Mach-O arm64/arm64e binaries `agent_a64[e]_30..90/plain.bin`, kernel bridges `kbridge_a64[e]_*`, and WebKit stagers `stager_a64_*` whose strings reference iOS private entitlements (`com.apple.private.security.storage.DiagnosticReports.read`), `JSEvaluateScript`, `IOSurfaceRoot`, `xnu-%d.%d.%d`, `sandbox_check`, and `/usr/libexec/corelliumd` — the shape of a WebKit-delivered iOS post-exploitation chain. A `setInterval` at ~60s forces `window.top.location.reload()` to re-run the staging path. The declared 'static assets' purpose does not match the shipped contents; the loader stages attacker-controlled code into any site that bundles it and delivers implants to end-user browsers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
